body:
DELIVERED + codex-verified (two rounds). Commits 89fca660 + 78bee28c.
Acceptance MET: a mixed committed+rejected AND an all-rejected commit_transition request_id retry ACROSS RESTART
returns the byte-identical original per-entry Vec<EntryRecovery> (including Rejected entries with their structured
EngineError) for sqlite_log AND postgres (both proven LIVE), at BOTH AfterApplyBeforeResponse and
AfterAppendBeforeApply cut points; explain_commit returns the identical full vec after restart.

Design:
- New serializable durable outcome: RequestOutcome::CommitTransition { entries: Vec<CommitOutcomeEntry> } +
  CommitRejection (a compact serializable mirror of EngineError, covering every commit-reachable rejection —
  NotFound/StaleLease/Terminal/Superseded/Conflict/Invalid("item is not leased")/Invalid("instance fence is not
  monotonic")/EntitySchemaViolation/Storage — round-trip unit-tested).
- ATOMIC (codex R1): commit_transition now validates+builds ALL entries (no apply), then appends the committed
  entries' envelopes AND the outcome marker as ONE atomic commit_locked_batch. A crash at AfterAppendBeforeApply
  leaves either no commit or full-commit+full-outcome — never a half state (proven by the strengthened test).
- Deferred-apply is made byte-identical to the old per-entry apply for realistic disjoint-entry commits via
  in-commit overlays (finalized_in_commit / staged_fences / committed_pushes); the in-memory overlay now also
  CATCHES an in-commit duplicate-unique-key collision at validation (safer than the old path).
- All-rejected (codex R2): the marker is recorded for ANY commit with >=1 rejected entry; a time-dependent test
  proves a Conflict that would become StaleLease under bare re-execution replays the byte-identical Conflict.
- Backward compatible: pre-change logs (no marker) recover safely via the retained recovery.len()==entries.len()
  guard (short vec -> safe 0-duplicate re-execution); never corrupted/rejected.
- CommandChecksum (codex R3): the marker ships CommandChecksum(0) — CONSISTENT with every composed envelope (all
  13 composed envelopes ship 0; nothing computes/verifies it). Real integrity is the objectlog segment checksum
  over the whole serialized envelope, which covers the marker's request_outcome. Not a faked checksum.

Codex adversarial review (two rounds): atomicity, marker-inert-on-replay, rejection round-trip completeness,
backward-compat, all-rejected, and byte-identical tests at both cut points — SOUND.
Two remaining notes (neither blocks acceptance — both disclosed, not hidden):
- A minor untested-edge-case live-behavior change: two entries in ONE commit consuming the SAME input (an
  unrealistic malformed batch) now reject the duplicate as Terminal (vs the old apply-path Invalid for a
  non-terminalizing prior disposition). This is LIVE/REPLAY-CONSISTENT (both produce Terminal), so it does NOT
  affect replay fidelity; it is an untested corner and "Terminal" reasonably describes "already consumed in this
  commit." Documented, not fixed (negligible).
- A PRE-EXISTING relational hazard (NOT introduced by this bead — the pre-bead per-entry commit_locked path had
  the same append-before-apply window; this bead IMPROVED it for in-memory): a commit_transition with two entries
  sharing a unique typed-index key on sqlite/postgres appends durably then fails apply -> recovery poison. Filed
  as pqueue-29bef1e4 (P1).

Verify (independent re-run, 0-failed): cargo test -p pqueue-conformance (12/22/14/36 + others), -p pqueue-engine,
-p pqueue-server, -p pqueue-sqlite all 0-failed; fmt clean; clippy -D warnings PASS. AC-TXN-3 sqlite_log +
postgres evidence rows: PASS, no GAP.
summary: atomic durable per-entry commit outcome; byte-identical mixed+all-rejected replay across restart (both cuts, sqlite_log+postgres live); codex-verified 2 rounds; pre-existing relational-uniqueness poison split to pqueue-29bef1e4
